memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid his hands on him. So the Israelites listened to him and did what the Lord had commanded Moses." — Deut 34:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses was gone, but God's work did not stop — because God had already prepared the next leader. Joshua "was filled with the spirit of wisdom," equipped and ready to lead the people forward. What a comfort this must have been. The people had lost their beloved leader, yet they were not left leaderless. God had provided, ensuring that His purposes would continue into the new generation.

This reveals a steadying truth about God's work: it never depends on any single person, and it never comes to a halt when one servant's time is done. God is always preparing the next leader, the next generation, the next chapter. His purposes march on, carried by those He raises up and equips. No leader is indispensable, because the Lord Himself is the one who leads.

There is great freedom in this. We can pour ourselves out in service without the crushing weight of thinking everything depends on us. When our season ends, God will raise up others. And we can trust Him with the future of His work, knowing He is always at work preparing what comes next.

Notice too that Joshua was equipped by God's Spirit for the task ahead. The same is true for us — God does not call without equipping. And ultimately, this points beyond every human leader to Jesus, whose name in Hebrew is the same as Joshua's, and who is the true and final Leader of God's people (Heb 4:8-9). Human leaders come and go, but Christ leads His people forever. Rest in Him, the Leader who never passes away.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I trust that God's work doesn't depend on any one person, including me?
2. How does knowing God always prepares the next generation free me?
3. Am I resting in Christ, the Leader who never passes away?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that Your work never stops, and that You always prepare those who come next. Free me from thinking everything depends on me, and help me rest in Christ, my Leader forever. Equip me for what You call me to. Amen.
